prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Official domains: meritbeauty.com
Recipient: the marketing team

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.meritbeauty.com/pages/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2021 | published: unknown
"0 items Your Bag is Empty Continue Shopping # About Us Founded in 2021, MERIT is a modern beauty brand that simplifies what it takes to get ready. Born out of an industry crowded with fleeting trends and products that demanded expert-level skills, MERIT was created as the antidote — a considered collection designed to bring ease to your everyday. With a timeless perspective on beauty and a commitment to uncompromising quality, we create beauty and lifestyle essentials that become signatures of your routine — products you’ll reach for daily and live with for years to come. MERIT is a global brand with teams in New York, Los Angeles, Toronto, London, and Paris."

[P2] source: https://www.meritbeauty.com/pages/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Shop Shop All Bestsellers Sets Leaving Soon ## The Signature Bag — free with your first order * Makeup Shop All Makeup Complexion Cheeks Lips Eyes Sets"

[P3] source: https://www.breef.com/breefingroom/long-articles/inside-merits-discipline-the-brand-making-minimalism-a-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The CMO Who Still Reviews Every Social Post Most beauty brands talk about social media like it's a distribution channel. Post here, spend there, measure reach, optimize CPM. MERIT treats it like the actual ground floor of the brand which means the most senior marketing leader in the building is in the room when content gets made. That's not a given. At most companies of MERIT's size and scale, the CMO is reviewing decks, not approving individual posts. Morin does both. She came up in the early days of Instagram, ran MERIT's social accounts herself at launch and five years later, with the brand at $100M and growing, she still sits in every single social review."

[P4] source: https://www.breef.com/breefingroom/long-articles/inside-merits-discipline-the-brand-making-minimalism-a-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Why Launching Less is Actually Harder Than it Looks Here’s a question the beauty industry rarely asks: what if you launched less? Not as an aesthetic choice, but as a business strategy. The norm is a new SKU every four to six weeks. It feeds the content machine, satisfies retailers who want novelty on shelves and keeps paid social campaigns refreshed. It also creates a kind of organizational ADD — every new launch pulls attention from the last one, and hero products never get the sustained marketing investment they’d need to become icons. MERIT’s development process (by contrast) takes years rather than months."

[P5] source: https://www.breef.com/breefingroom/long-articles/inside-merits-discipline-the-brand-making-minimalism-a-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Which means by the time something launches, the story isn't being retrofitted around the formula, it’s already fully formed. Most brand teams work in reverse (and you can feel it). Product emerges from the lab, gets handed to marketing three months before launch, and the team scrambles to build a narrative around something they had no hand in shaping. The result is content that feels disconnected (because it is). MERIT's sequence solves for that at the source. Samples of four shades of pink lipstick with smudges on white paper and containers above them. Various lipstick swatches on paper with lipsticks and labels showing shade names and tones."

[P6] source: https://www.accio.com/biz-company/meritbeauty | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Desiree Design Studio The Merit Method: Beauty Without the Fuss Merit's digital marketing strategy is robust, leveraging platforms like Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Pinterest to reach a broad audience. Sephora Merit Clean Makeup by Katherine Power Simplify your routine with MERIT's selection of minimalist-friendly formulas. Discover dependable makeup, skincare, brushes, and more. MERIT Beauty About MERIT Beauty: Clean Beauty Brand MERIT offers Clean, Vegan, Cruelty-free beauty products. We take a holistic approach to clean by creating safe products for your skin and the planet. The New York Times We Tested Every Product From Merit Beauty. The Truth ..."

[P7] source: https://www.beautyexpert-consulting.com/post/beauty-brand-launch-france-merit-case-study | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Phase 4: execution partner curation Getting the strategy right is one thing. Executing it is where the right partners come in. We put together a shortlist of top-tier French and European agencies across three areas: * Digital marketing: agencies that know premium beauty and deliver on paid social. * PR & influence: teams with real relationships in beauty media and genuine influencer networks. * Creative & content: partners whose aesthetic matches Merit's minimalist universe. For each one, we included a detailed brief and selection criteria, which made Merit's final choice far more straightforward. > CEO, Merit Beauty \"The team at Beauty Expert Consulting were true partners in our launch."

[P8] source: https://www.meritbeauty.com/pages/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Shade Matching, Made Simple Find My Shade ## The Signature Bag — free with your first order The following text field filters the results that follow as you type."

[P9] source: https://www.beautyexpert-consulting.com/post/beauty-brand-launch-france-merit-case-study | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The challenge: launching a digital beauty brand in France Merit Beauty had built a remarkable success in the American digital space. Its DNA was crystal clear: \"Effective & Aesthetic Makeup\", that rare sweet spot between real performance and beautiful minimalism. But entering French retail is the haute couture exam of the beauty world. One wrong move and credibility suffers. Go too broad with distribution and you dilute what makes you special; not selective enough and you miss the point. Merit's question was deceptively simple: > How do we keep our cult digital brand identity intact while building an elite physical presence in > France?"

[P10] source: https://www.meritbeauty.com/blogs/stories | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Shop Shop All Bestsellers Sets Leaving Soon Get the Look ## The Signature Bag — free with your first order ## The Holiday Gift Edit Shop Gifts * Makeup Shop All Makeup Complexion Cheeks Lips Eyes Sets"
